text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's prime minister Zhan Videnov won on Tuesday a confidence vote from the Supreme Council of his party and postponed any cabinet reshuffle until a party congress on December 21-22.

-- Bulgaria's biggest opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) plans to discuss the International Monetary Fund's proposal to introduce a currency board in the country with representatives of local political parties and international institutions, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- The UDF plans to press for changes in the boards of the Bulgarian National Bank and the State Savings Bank because these institutions should take full responsibility for the current banking crisis, Ivan Kostov said.
-- Ballistic tests proved a gun found near the murder site of Bulgaria's ex-premier Andrei Lukanov was used in the crime, Sofia City chief prosecutor Nestor Nestorov said.
Lukanov was shot dead in front of his home in Sofia on October 2.

-- Bulgaria's state transport companies have posted 154 million levs profit after taxes for the first nine months of 1996 against 1.6 billion levs losses for the same period of 1995, transport ministry officials said.

-- The European Investment Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and other international financial institutions are expected to provide some $170 million for the reconstruction of Sofia airport to be carried out by Bulgaria's state construction company Glavbolgarstroy, Transport Minister Stamen Stamenov said.

-- The EBRD approved a two-year strategy for Bulgaria, which includes active support for private businesses and investment of some 24.3 million Ecus in the privatisation and recapitalisation of state owned United Bulgarian Bank.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) opposes the introduction of a currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund before other options to stabilise the country's economy are considered, BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said.
-- Bulgaria's Conferderation of Independent Trade Unions (CITU) plans to stage a 24-hour nationwide strike on December 4 to trigger early parliamentary elections in 1997, a union official said.
-- Bulgaria bought 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina for a December-May delivery.
